learning_outcomes.text: Knowledge and skills to apply the scientific and technological fundamentals of oleohydraulics and pneumatics.

syllabus_topics: Pneumatics: Introduction. Fundamentals of pneumatics. Symbology
Pneumatics: Production, distribution and treatment of compressed air. Pipes and fittings.
Pneumatics: Actuators (cylinders, rotary actuators, grippers and motors).
Pneumatics: Directional and control valves. Regulation, control and blocking.
Pneumatics: Actuator governance and control. Pneumatic circuits. Diagrams.
Hydraulics: Fluid transport and distribution systems. Power systems. Fundamentals of oleohydraulics.
Hydraulics: Oleohydraulic fluids. Positive displacement pumps.
teaching_methods: Theoretical study of the course program content
Development of practical questions and problems related to theoretical aspects
Development of a practical project based on a topic agreed upon with the teaching team, using catalogs and real manufacturer data
assessment_rules: The final course grade (CF) is calculated using the formula: CF = 0.5 * CPP + 0.05 * CED + 0.4 * CTF + 0.05 * CP, where CPP is the in-person exam grade, CED is the continuous assessment grade, CTF is the final project grade, and CP is the practices grade. The in-person exam consists of two theory questions and two practical problems, and a minimum grade of 4 (out of 10) is required on this exam for the continuous assessment grade (PEC) to be considered. It is mandatory to have correctly completed the practices to pass the course. The final project must be delivered no later than the week following the last exam week.
